thread:
mina: quick update from the Harbinger-embed-v1 bring-up. did int8pc and fp16 baselines across the wiki-q and shortquery holdouts. dropping notes here for triage.

mina: TL;DR: overall recall@5 ~same; recall@1 regression concentrated on <5-token queries and multi-intent tiny queries. per-channel int8 recovers most but not all.

tj: good context. which datasets/splits? and run env?

mina: ran on wiki-q (10k queries) and shortquery-holdout (3k queries, avg len 4.2). infra: cpu encoding on host, runtime kernels = xla-int8-pc. eval flags below.

mina: eval command:
```bash
python -m evals.embeddings \
  --model harbinger-embed-v1 \
  --quant int8_pc \
  --datasets wiki_q,shortquery_holdout \
  --batch 1024 \
  --metric recall@k
```

harry: numbers pls. a quick table is fine.

mina: paste of key rows:
```
model                 dataset                r@1    r@5    r@10
harbinger-fp16        wiki_q                0.661  0.853  0.893
harbinger-int8pc      wiki_q                0.657  0.850  0.891
harbinger-fp16        shortquery_holdout    0.592  0.782  0.841
harbinger-int8pc      shortquery_holdout    0.542  0.780  0.838
```

mina: so r@1 drop is ~5pp on short queries for int8pc vs fp16. r@5 stable.

katie: ouch at r@1. do we see embedding norms or cosine gap shifts?

mina: yes. mean norm change small (~0.02) but cosine-gap (top1 - top2) decreased on failures: fp16 avg gap 0.18, int8pc 0.09 for the affected subset. attached small csv in ticket.

tj: could be quant noise causing tie/flip at top1. do we have examples?

mina: short examples:
```
q1: "cancel"         fp16_rank1_item=A  cos_top1=0.77  int8pc_rank1_item=B  cos_top1=0.63
q2: "billing"        fp16_rank1_item=C  cos_top1=0.82  int8pc_rank1_item=C  cos_top1=0.81
q3: "change plan"    fp16_rank1_item=D  cos_top1=0.69  int8pc_rank1_item=E  cos_top1=0.61
```

mina: notice some stable ones (billing) but several flips.

harry: maybe we should compute a confidence metric (cosine gap) and route low-confidence short queries to fp16. cheaper than always using fp16.

katie: agree. any idea about cost impact? also can we try post-quant calibration (per-cluster scale) instead?

mina: rough sim: short queries ~9% of traffic. routing those to fp16 for fallback yields ~6% ops cost uplift but restores ~3.4pp r@1 on global traffic.

tj: calibration could be promising but trickier at runtime. what's the kernel difference for short seqs? any padding issues or different attention math?

mina: I profiled and found the int8 kernel's reduction path uses a different accumulation order causing tiny fp error magnification when seq_len<8. adding forced pad to 8 reduced failures by ~40%. so padding fudge helps.

harry: so options: 1) routing low-confidence short queries to fp16, 2) force min-pad=8 in quant kernels for short queries, 3) improve quant (6bit per-channel?) sweep.

katie: can we do a quick A/B: pad-to-8 vs routing vs baseline, measure r@1 and cost? then pick a rollout rule.

mina: yes. I'll spin experiments: pad-to-8 variant + int6pc sweep (6/8-bit), and run human eval on the top-3 changed hits.

qa-bot: scheduled eval job: emb-eval-4298765432-pad8 (ETA ~3h).

mina: I'll attach the csv and a short checklist to ticket ML-ONB-999. Please add anyone who should review human eval.

tj: tagging infra for potential runtime pad change if results look good @infra-team

harry: also consider adding a rollout signal: if cosine_gap<0.12 and tokens<=5 then fallback. write down in ticket.

mina: noted. thanks all, will report back with the three-arm comparison and cost sims. :rocket:
